notes.n3.servers: Taiwanese ODMs (Foxconn, Quanta, Wiwynn) build most hyperscaler AI racks; Dell, HPE, Supermicro and Lenovo serve enterprise, sovereign and neocloud buyers.
notes.n3.network: NVIDIA (InfiniBand + Spectrum-X) and Arista lead AI back-end networking, with Cisco, Celestica white-box and HPE-Juniper following; Ethernet is gaining share over InfiniBand.
notes.n3.optics: Chinese vendors InnoLight and Eoptolink lead 800G/1.6T transceiver volume, with Coherent, Lumentum and Fabrinet the main Western suppliers; AECs (Credo) take short in-rack links.
notes.n3.storage: AI-native vendors (VAST at $30B valuation in Mar 2026, WEKA, DDN) compete with Dell, NetApp, Pure and IBM; KV-cache offload is the new battleground.
notes.n3.opt: Liquid-cooled racks are now standard for GB200-class systems; KV-cache offload to flash (NVIDIA ICMS, Pliops, WEKA, VAST) and optical I/O are emerging efficiency levers.
notes.n3.scaleup: NVLink dominates; UALink and Broadcom scale-up Ethernet are the open alternatives
notes.n3.rackpower: Shift to 800 VDC with Delta and Lite-On supplying MGX power racks
notes.n3.mgmt: NVIDIA Mission Control/BCM bundled with DGX; open tools (MAAS, Slurm) elsewhere
notes.n3.refurb: Young market: H100/A100 resale marketplaces launched in 2026 as Blackwell displaces Hopper
